messages:

Cc: Monica Ruiz <monica.ruiz@heliocorp.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Dedicated capacity for HelioCorp launch (Dec-Jan)

Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward with a dedicated pool to support our inference workloads for HelioCorp Mobile Customer Personalization (MCP). Target go-live: 2027-01-15. Initial sizing request in the attached RFP: ~12 A100-equivalent slots, burst to 20 for peak windows.

Key asks:
- Minimum guaranteed throughput of 120 tokens/sec for the highest-priority route
- 99.9% availability for weekdays 06:00-22:00 PT
- Data residency in us-west-2

Can you confirm whether that fits Redwood Dedicated's current capacity and what lead times we should expect? We need a mutual action plan and a rough cost estimate to present to procurement by Dec 17.

Thanks,
Carlos
---
Carlos Mendez
Head of Platform Engineering, HelioCorp

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos@heliocorp.com>
Cc: Monica Ruiz <monica.ruiz@heliocorp.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated capacity for HelioCorp launch (Dec-Jan)

Carlos —
Appreciate the clear requirements and the RFP. High level: we can provision a Dedicated pool that meets the throughput and residency asks, but there are two constraints I want to flag up front so you have full transparency.

1) We have a queued request from Astra Labs (deal queued earlier this month) that targets the same us-west-2 tranche and requests an overlapping burst window around your go-live.
2) Q4 hardware deliveries and a planned maintenance in early Jan reduce our immediate headroom for A100-equivalent slots.

Options I recommend (shortlist):
- Option A (preferred): Reserve 12 slots now from our Reserved Burst lane; schedule a canary rollout 2027-01-10 and rely on short-term burst to 20 for 4 peak days. This requires a signed commitment by Dec 17.
- Option B (split): Guarantee 9 dedicated slots + autoscale to 20 using mixed-quantized variants for non-critical routes (saves cost, needs evaluation).
- Option C (deferred start): Push go-live to 2027-01-25 to avoid the Astra contention and maintenance window.

I'll put a request into Capacity Ops to map current headroom and surface a heatmap; attaching the Astra request we're reconciling. Can you confirm which option you'd prefer? I'll escalate internally once you pick a path so we can lock scheduling and SLA exceptions.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachment: —
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: URGENT: HelioCorp request collides with Astra Labs queued deal — capacity decision needed

Team —
Looping you in to request immediate capacity guidance and a recommended prioritization approach. Summary: HelioCorp (RWI-2026-HELI-045) needs 12 A100-equivalent slots with burst to 20 for go-live 2027-01-15. Astra Labs (queued deal) has requested 10 slots with overlapping burst windows the week of Jan 10–20; Astra was queued before Helio's inbound RFP. Hardware deliveries + planned maintenance reduce spare headroom to roughly ~18 effective slots in us-west-2 during the contested window.

Constraints and consequences:
- If we grant both full bursts simultaneously we exceed headroom and risk SLA degradation across both accounts.
- Preempting Astra without a contractual lever risks churn and legal exposure; Astra is on a pre-commit but not yet signed.

Questions:
1) Can Capacity Ops re-run the heatmap and tell us: which physical hosts/tranches are involved, and whether short-term rebalancing across other regions (with cross-region routing) is viable without violating data residency?
2) What's the minimum burst we can safely expose to Helio while preserving a baseline for Astra (if we choose to share)?
3) If we must choose, what prioritization policy do we apply: first-come queued deals, signed commitments, ARR tier, or strategic account (Helio is enterprise with SSO + compliance needs)?

Suggested immediate actions: reroute a 4-slot cold pool from a lower-priority tranche, offer Helio Option B (split) as temporary, and open a short-term SLA credit buffer to Helio if we take Option C.

Attaching Astra's request and the fleet heatmap I pulled from the console. Can you triage today so I can respond to Helio by EOD?

—Rafael
attachment: Astra_capacity_request.xlsx, fleet-heatmap-q4.png
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: URGENT: HelioCorp request collides with Astra Labs queued deal — capacity decision needed

Rafael / all —
Thanks for the write-up and the artifacts. I re-ran the allocation heatmap and validated maintenance windows. Findings:
- us-west-2 tranche alpha (hosts a, b, c) can flex by +6 slots if we temporarily shift low-priority sandbox workloads to reserved hosts in us-east-1 and enable cross-region routing for non-PHI routes. That preserves data residency for routes marked as "us-only" but requires a config change and falls back to reduced throughput for cross-region traffic.
- If both Helio and Astra require full burst simultaneously, we will exceed thermal headroom during the maintenance window and risk token-level throttling.

Recommendation (fast path):
1) Offer Helio Option B (guarantee 9 dedicated + autoscale to 18 using quantized variants) as the initial commitment.
2) Ask Helio to sign a 6-week short-term burst addendum at a premium (this secures the remaining +3 burst slots on alpha tranche for 4 peak days). This preserves Astra's queued allocation until Astra either signs or is re-prioritized.
3) If Helio pushes for full 12+burst immediately, we escalate to commercial for a temporary priority credit and propose a scheduled blue/green cutover that minimizes overlap with Astra's burst window.

I'll open the formal change request in the capacity tracker and tag infra on the config change for sandbox migration. Rafael — please relay the Option B proposal to Helio and request written sign-off by Dec 17 if they want the short-burst addendum.

—Soojin
Head of Capacity, Redwood Inference
